causal_chain: Better separation of supportive versus misleading collaborative evidence improves full-sort ranking quality, especially for ambiguous and long-tail targets.
Scoring candidates with direct affinity plus excited transport minus inhibited transport raises preference-consistent items and demotes popularity-driven or mixed-taste false positives.
Splitting this residual structure into excitation and inhibition graphs gives separate collaborative evidence for 'go-together' and 'should-not-follow-from-this-history' item signals.
Train-only user histories define item-item residual relations after subtracting popularity-expected co-occurrence.
User-conditioned gating over historical items selects which signed graph paths are relevant for the current user's latent intent.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that forms each user's score through a signed residual propagation state over item-item transitions, with separate excitation and inhibition operators gated by the user's latent intent, will rank held-out items better than static interaction scoring because it can amplify coherent co-consumption evidence while actively suppressing misleading associations created by popularity and mixed-taste histories.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from adding an item-item graph side channel or extra parameters rather than from the signed residual excitation/inhibition mechanism itself.
discriminative_predictions: Against a matched unsigned-transport control with the same embeddings and graph budget, the signed model should show larger NDCG@10 gains for users whose training histories span multiple popularity bands or mixed genres.
If the mechanism is real, improvement should be stronger on tail and mid-popularity held-out items than on head items dominated by direct-affinity baselines.
Randomly flipping residual-edge signs or collapsing positive/negative graphs into a single unsigned graph should reduce any benefit if signed separation is the causal mechanism.
Removing the inhibition channel while keeping excitation should increase scores for popular false positives more than for true held-out positives.
expected_evidence: Ablation to mechanism-off direct-affinity scoring loses any gains attributable to transport.
Matched-control comparison to unsigned transport isolates whether signed inhibition matters beyond generic graph smoothing.
Per-item-bucket and per-user-history-diversity slices show whether benefits concentrate where misleading co-occurrence is most plausible.
Qualification runs complete within the frozen ML-1M protocol using a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender.
research_spec.falsifier: If a parameter-matched unsigned transport control matches or exceeds the signed residual model, and inhibition ablations do not selectively worsen popular false-positive ranking, then the signed excitation/inhibition hypothesis is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This candidate changes the core relation from user-item matching alone to signed item-item residual transport, changes the model structure by introducing dual propagation channels and user-conditioned gating, and changes the interaction structure by scoring through history-dependent graph transport rather than a static embedding match.
research_spec.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that builds train-only signed residual item-item graphs, propagates each user's historical signal through separate excitation and inhibition channels, and gates those channels by user intent will improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over static collaborative filters and unsigned transport controls because it can amplify preference-consistent collaborative paths while subtracting misleading popularity-shaped associations.

research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a dual-channel signed residual propagation scorer: build positive and negative residual item-item graphs from train histories, aggregate a user's history through both graphs with learned attention, then combine direct affinity, positive transport, and subtractive negative transport in the ranking score.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Set excitation and inhibition transport coefficients to zero and score only by direct user-item affinity with the same embeddings and pairwise training loop, leaving all graph-derived channels inactive.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: Add a train-only signed residual item-item transport module with separate positive and negative channels to a pairwise collaborative scorer, and test whether this outperforms the same scorer with graph channels removed or collapsed to unsigned transport.

causal_chain: A small set of persistent user intent slots can preserve separable preference modes across the interaction history.
Event-conditioned transport between intent slots lets recent items reweight which latent mode is active without requiring session labels or held-out access.
Reduced mode averaging should improve ranking of held-out items, especially for users with diverse histories, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 than static single-vector collaborative filters.
Scoring candidates by the best-supported intent slot plus a disagreement penalty against conflicting slots reduces averaging over incompatible interests.
Users with mixed tastes are poorly summarized by a single static embedding.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain may come only from increased parameter count or regularization side effects rather than from multi-state transport and disagreement-aware routing.
discriminative_predictions: Ablating cross-slot transport while keeping multiple slots should reduce performance more than merely shrinking embedding dimension, indicating that dynamic routing rather than capacity alone matters.

Compared with a matched single-embedding control of similar parameter scale, the proposed model should show larger NDCG@10 improvement on users with longer or more diverse histories than on very short-history users.
The disagreement penalty should help ranking of substitute-like or niche positives that would otherwise be suppressed by averaging across incompatible user interests.
expected_evidence: Mechanism-off ablations can isolate the contribution of multi-slot memory, event-conditioned transport, and disagreement-aware scoring.

causal_chain: If gains disappear when coalition competition is removed under a matched control, the frontier mechanism is likely unnecessary.
If scoring also includes an explicit conflict term against non-selected coalitions, candidates that match one taste while contradicting another can be separated from broadly compatible items.

If the model decomposes each user's training history into a small set of learned latent coalitions, different candidate items can route to different coalitions instead of competing through one global preference vector.
This coalition-routing plus conflict suppression should improve ordering of ambiguous and multi-intent cases in full-sort ranking.
Users in ML-1M often have mixed tastes that are poorly summarized by a single embedding or uniform history pool.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any observed improvement may come only from increased parameter count and a history-attention encoder, not from coalition competition or the explicit conflict channel.
discriminative_predictions: Compared with a matched mechanism-off version that uses the same history encoder but only supportive aggregation, the frontier model should show larger gains for users with more diverse training histories than for users with short concentrated histories.
If coalition competition is the real driver, ablating only the conflict term should remove a substantial fraction of the frontier advantage while leaving parameter count nearly unchanged.

The frontier model should assign lower scores than the mechanism-off control to candidates that strongly align with one inferred taste coalition while conflicting with another coalition built from the same user history.
expected_evidence: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender can train under pairwise BPR-style input using only train-split user histories and full-sort evaluation.
A matched control with identical embedding sizes and history encoder but no coalition competition should narrow or erase gains if the proposed mechanism is not causal.
Full-sort NDCG@10 stratified by user history diversity should favor the frontier model more strongly in high-diversity strata than in low-diversity strata.
Inspection of routing weights should show candidate-specific concentration on different user coalitions rather than a nearly uniform reuse of the same pooled representation.
research_spec.falsifier: If a matched mechanism-off control with the same embeddings, history encoder, and parameter budget matches or exceeds the frontier model on full-sort NDCG@10 overall and on high-diversity-user slices, then the coalition-competition hypothesis is falsified.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the core user representation from a single vector or graph-smoothed vector into a candidate-routed set of latent history coalitions, adds a new support-versus-conflict interaction structure at scoring time, and requires custom executable capability for coalition construction and competitive routing that is not available in the current profile catalog.
research_spec.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that represents each user's training history as a small set of latent taste coalitions, then scores each candidate by routing to its most supportive coalition while subtracting conflict from rival coalitions, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over conventional single-channel collaborative filtering because it can preserve mixed preferences without collapsing them into one static compatibility signal.

causal_chain: A candidate-conditioned support router can upweight the specific historical items that justify a candidate instead of collapsing the whole history into one static user vector.
A parallel inhibition router can learn which historical items provide counter-evidence for a candidate, separating weak relevance from active mismatch.
Combining direct affinity, routed support, and routed inhibition yields more selective full-sort scores than static embedding matching.

More selective scores should improve ranking of held-out items, especially for users with diverse histories and for candidates that are neither globally popular nor nearest to the user's average taste.
Users with mixed-taste histories contain only a subset of past items that are relevant to any given candidate item.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that learns which historical interactions most support each positive target and explicitly trains ranking margins to remain stable when those support interactions are removed will generalize better in offline top-n recommendation than a matched model trained only on factual pairwise ranking, because it suppresses brittle shortcut co-occurrence reliance and promotes support-distributed user representations.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from increased parameter count or extra history aggregation capacity rather than from the distinct support-versus-inhibition routing mechanism.
discriminative_predictions: If the inhibition channel is mechanistically useful, removing only the inhibition route should hurt ranking on hard-candidate contrasts more than removing an equal number of parameters elsewhere.

Relative to a matched mechanism-off control with the same base embeddings and pairwise loss, the routed model should show larger gains for users with longer or more diverse training histories than for users with very short histories.

The routed model should assign higher attention concentration to a small subset of history items for each scored candidate, while the mechanism-off control cannot produce candidate-specific support redistribution.
expected_evidence: A measurable ablation gap between full dual-route scoring and attraction-only scoring, indicating that inhibition is contributing beyond simple history attention.
Improved full-sort NDCG@10 over the matched mechanism-off control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Per-candidate support weights that vary meaningfully across candidates for the same user rather than collapsing to near-uniform averages.
research_spec.falsifier: If a matched control that replaces candidate-conditioned support and inhibition routing with a single uniform or candidate-independent history summary matches or exceeds the proposed model's NDCG@10, the frontier claim is not supported.

It introduces a new interaction structure in which each candidate is scored through target-conditioned routing over the user's full training history with separate evidence-for and evidence-against channels. That requires custom history retrieval, dual attention operators, and a new scoring composition unavailable in the current executable profile operators.

causal_chain: A disagreement-aware gate that downweights diffuse or conflicting prototype assignments prevents prototype averaging from collapsing back to a single-vector scorer.

An anti-collapse pairwise regularizer that rewards separation of active prototypes maintains distinct intent channels, allowing full-sort scoring to surface items aligned with minority but real user interests.
Representing each user as a small mixture over latent intent prototypes preserves multiple concurrent preference modes without requiring sequence supervision or side data.

Routing positive and negative items through prototype-specific compatibility exposes which intent supports the observed pairwise comparison instead of forcing all comparisons through one shared user state.
Single-embedding collaborative filters compress mixed user taste into one vector, causing conflicting historical signals to cancel when scoring candidates.

Therefore a prototype-mixture, disagreement-gated pairwise recommender should improve ranking of held-out items for mixed-taste users relative to static single-representation baselines under the same offline protocol.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that represents each user and item as adaptive mixtures over multiple latent prototypes, then scores a pair through disagreement-aware prototype routing and a residual anti-collapse pairwise objective, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 by capturing multi-intent user preference and context-free item facet diversity that single-embedding pairwise matrix-factorization-style mechanisms cannot express.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from increased parameter count and regularization rather than true multi-intent routing; a wider latent space might help even without prototype disagreement mechanisms.
discriminative_predictions: A mechanism-off variant that keeps prototypes but removes disagreement-aware routing should show higher prototype usage entropy collapse and weaker ranking gains, indicating that routing rather than parameter count is responsible.

Compared with a matched single-embedding MF control at similar embedding budget, improvements should concentrate on users whose histories span multiple item neighborhoods rather than being uniform across all users.

If prototype anti-collapse regularization is removed, learned prototype assignments should become redundant and full-sort NDCG@10 should regress toward the matched control despite similar training loss.
expected_evidence: Per-user analysis shows larger benefit for users with more internally diverse historical item neighborhoods.
Prototype assignment statistics show multiple active user intents for a non-trivial subset of users rather than universal single-prototype dominance.

research_spec.falsifier: If the full model fails to beat both a matched single-embedding control and the mechanism-off ablation, or if learned prototype assignments collapse to near-single-prototype usage for almost all users, the hypothesis is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This changes the core representation and interaction structure from one user embedding and one item embedding to user/item prototype mixtures with disagreement-gated routing and explicit anti-collapse training. The mechanism is not a configuration tweak or simple operator addition to the active profile families; it introduces a new executable capability for multi-intent prototype composition inside a GeneralRecommender.
research_spec.hypothesis: A candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender that models each user and item as adaptive mixtures over shared latent prototypes, scores pairs through disagreement-aware prototype routing, and trains with a prototype anti-collapse pairwise objective will improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over matched single-representation collaborative filtering because it can preserve and selectively activate multiple preference modes that static embeddings cannot represent.

causal_chain: A small bank of user preference states lets the model store distinct taste modes instead of averaging them.
Event-conditioned transport updates the state bank by routing each observed positive interaction to the most compatible state and softly diffusing information to nearby states.
This reduces interference from unrelated historical items and improves ranking of held-out items under full-sort evaluation.
Users in ML-1M often mix multiple stable tastes, so collapsing history into one embedding causes incompatible signals to cancel.
When scoring a candidate item, the model uses disagreement-aware routing over the user state bank so only the relevant taste states dominate the score.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain may come only from increased parameter count or extra nonlinearity rather than from explicit multi-state transport and disagreement-aware routing.
discriminative_predictions: Ablating disagreement-aware routing while keeping the same state bank should reduce performance more on users whose histories span distant item neighborhoods.

Compared with a matched single-state control, the multi-state transport model should show larger gains for users with more diverse interaction histories than for users with highly concentrated histories.
State usage entropy should be higher for mixed-taste users, and those users should contribute a disproportionate share of any ranking improvement.

research_spec.falsifier: If a parameter-matched single-state control matches or exceeds the proposed model, and ablations show no meaningful dependence on multi-state transport or disagreement-aware routing, the hypothesis is falsified.
research_spec.high_change_justification: The proposal replaces the core user representation from one static embedding to a structured memory of multiple persistent states with event-conditioned transport and routing. This changes model structure, interaction structure, and training semantics rather than adjusting an existing loss weight or propagation depth.
research_spec.hypothesis: A candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender that represents each user as a small bank of persistent latent preference states, updates those states with event-conditioned transport from observed positive items, and scores candidates through disagreement-aware routing over the state bank will outperform matched single-state collaborative filtering on ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 because it preserves multiple tastes without forcing them into one embedding.

research_spec.resource_hypothesis: The model should fit within the stated development budget because ML-1M is small and the added cost is a modest K-fold expansion of user-side state tensors plus routing operations, all implementable with standard PyTorch tensor ops in a single candidate-local GeneralRecommender.

causal_chain: A separate veto channel can learn which historical interactions imply mismatch or substitution conflict for that same candidate, producing explicit subtractive evidence instead of forcing all disagreement into weak low-affinity scores.

Because held-out ranking on ML-1M contains many users with mixed histories, separating support from veto and enforcing support robustness should improve ranking of candidates that are locally consistent with part of a user's taste while suppressing candidates that only match popularity or the wrong taste facet.

Candidate-conditioned cross-attention over a user's historical items can identify which past interactions provide positive evidence for a queried candidate rather than collapsing all history into one static user vector.

Training the model to preserve pairwise margins when its top support evidences are partially masked discourages brittle reliance on one shortcut co-occurrence and promotes distributed collaborative support.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that learns which historical interactions most support each positive target and explicitly trains ranking margins to remain stable when those support interactions are removed will generalize better in offline top-n recommendation than a matched model trained only on factual pairwise ranking, because it suppresses brittle shortcut co-occurrence reliance and promotes support-distributed user representations.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from increased parameter count or a generic history-attention effect rather than from the specific dual support-versus-veto decomposition and support-masking stability objective.
discriminative_predictions: If performance gains are only due to popularity smoothing or extra capacity, improvements should concentrate on head items and should not persist under a parameter-matched attentive additive-history control without the veto channel and masking objective.

If support-robustness is causal, the proposed model should show smaller NDCG@10 degradation than a matched attentive-history control when a few high-attention historical interactions are ablated at evaluation-time scoring.

If the support/veto decomposition is causal, removing only the veto channel while keeping parameter count similar should reduce improvement most strongly for users with diverse or internally conflicting histories.
expected_evidence: Ablation of the support-masking stability term reduces robustness to history-item removal and weakens any ranking gain on mixed-taste users.
Compared with a parameter-matched attentive-history pairwise control, the full model improves full-sort NDCG@10 on the frozen ML-1M split.
Dual-channel attention diagnostics show that promoted and vetoed history items differ systematically for the same user-candidate pair rather than collapsing to the same support pattern.
research_spec.falsifier: If a parameter-matched control that uses candidate-conditioned history attention but no explicit veto channel and no support-masking stability matches or exceeds the proposed model on full-sort NDCG@10, the frontier claim is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This is not a parameter or tuning variation of BPR_MF or existing LightGCN descendants. It changes the scoring object from static user-item compatibility to candidate-conditioned evidence routing over user history, introduces a new negative collaborative relation via veto evidence, and adds a counterfactual stability objective requiring custom executable logic beyond current profile operators.
research_spec.hypothesis: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender that scores each user-item pair through dual candidate-conditioned set encoders over the user's interaction history—one promotive support channel and one subtractive veto channel—and that regularizes pairwise margins to remain stable under masking of top support interactions will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over static pairwise collaborative filters on the frozen ML-1M protocol.
implementation_requirements: Add a support-masking consistency term that recomputes the positive-item score after masking a small subset of highest-support history items and penalizes excessive pairwise margin collapse.
Define score(u,i)=base_user_item_affinity + support_score(u,i) - veto_score(u,i), with pairwise BPR-style loss on positive and sampled negative items.
Implement a RecBole GeneralRecommender with pairwise training that caches each user's train-history item indices and a padded/truncated history tensor for minibatch lookup.
Provide candidate-local ablations for mechanism-off execution: no-veto/no-mask attentive control and optionally no-mask full model using the same training/evaluation pipeline.
Use shared item embeddings plus lightweight support-query and veto-query projections so a target item attends over a user's history twice, producing promotive and subtractive evidence summaries.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use a parameter-matched candidate-conditioned attentive-history pairwise recommender with the same embedding tables, history truncation, optimizer, and training loop, but collapse evidence to a single additive support channel and remove the support-masking consistency loss.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Replace static user representation scoring with dual candidate-conditioned historical evidence routing and counterfactual support-stability regularization.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Executable mechanism-off variant: keep the same item embeddings, candidate-conditioned history lookup, and pairwise training loop, but disable the veto channel and the support-masking consistency loss so scoring becomes base_user_item_affinity plus a single additive support-attention summary only.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: A dual-channel candidate-conditioned history-attention BPR recommender versus a parameter-matched single-channel attentive-history BPR control under identical frozen ML-1M full-sort evaluation.
research_spec.research_question: Does explicitly separating promotive and veto historical evidence for each candidate, plus enforcing support-robust pairwise margins, improve full-sort NDCG@10 beyond what can be achieved by ordinary static compatibility or single-channel attentive-history collaborative filtering under the frozen ML-1M protocol?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: A truncated-history implementation with shared projections and one masked re-score per positive pair should fit the development budget on ML-1M, because the dataset is moderate and the model avoids full graph propagation or large transformer stacks.

causal_chain: A separate exclusion prototype built from cross-slot disagreement can encode items that are near some historical evidence but inconsistent with the user's dominant co-occurring intents.
A small set of user-specific intent slots built from attention over historical item embeddings can preserve distinct preference modes during pairwise training.

At scoring time, routing a candidate through the best-matching intent slot while subtracting gated exclusion alignment should raise scores for coherent niche positives and lower scores for misleading broadly similar items.
This sharper intent-selection-plus-repulsion mechanism should improve full-sort NDCG@10 relative to a matched single-vector pairwise control.
Users in ML-1M often express multiple stable tastes that a single embedding compresses into an average preference vector.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come merely from using interaction-history aggregation at inference, producing a stronger user representation through extra capacity, rather than from the specific combination of multi-intent routing and exclusion subtraction.
discriminative_predictions: Compared with a mechanism-off mean-history dot-product control using the same item embeddings and pairwise optimizer, the proposed model should show larger improvement for users with longer and more diverse histories than for short-history users.

If multi-intent routing is causal, the winning intent slot for a user's held-out positives should vary meaningfully across candidates for mixed-taste users, whereas the mechanism-off control has no candidate-specific user-state selection.

If the exclusion channel is causal, score reductions should concentrate on popular or cross-genre distractor items that align with one intent slot but conflict with the routed slot, not uniformly across all negatives.
expected_evidence: Ablating exclusion while keeping multi-intent slots should reduce the benefit specifically on users whose histories span weakly compatible item clusters.
Higher full-sort NDCG@10 than the executable mechanism-off control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Positive items for mixed-history users receive higher routed-slot affinity than mean-history affinity, while common distractors receive stronger exclusion penalties.
research_spec.falsifier: If the matched mechanism-off control matches or exceeds NDCG@10, or if routed-slot assignments collapse to a single slot for most users with no measurable exclusion effect on distractor scores, the hypothesis is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This changes the core representation from one user embedding to a candidate-routed set of intent slots plus an explicit exclusion prototype, changes the interaction structure from static bilinear matching to slot selection with subtractive gating, and introduces a custom executable capability for per-user history-conditioned scoring absent from the active profile catalog.
research_spec.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that represents each user as a small mixture of intent slots derived from the user's historical items and scores each candidate through routed attraction minus a learned exclusion prototype will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over matched single-vector collaborative filtering because it preserves multi-interest structure while explicitly suppressing near-miss distractors.
implementation_requirements: Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender with user embeddings, item embeddings, K global intent query vectors, and an exclusion projection module in PyTorch.

Implement an executable mechanism-off sibling in the same file that replaces routed multi-slot scoring and exclusion subtraction with a single mean-history user representation dot product under the same optimizer and data flow.
Precompute each user's interacted item ids from the train matrix only and build user intent slots by attention pooling over that user's historical item embeddings during forward passes.
Provide full-sort prediction by batching users, recomputing or caching train-only intent slots, and scoring against all candidate item embeddings without reading held-out interactions.

Score a user-item pair by computing candidate-conditioned routing weights over the K intent slots, taking the routed attraction score, subtracting a sigmoid-gated exclusion alignment term, and training with BPR loss.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use the same train matrix, item embedding dimensionality, optimizer family, pairwise loss, regularization budget style, and evaluation pipeline as the proposed model, differing only by collapsing the representation to a single mean-history vector and removing exclusion gating.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Replace static user scoring with a history-conditioned multi-intent slot constructor plus candidate-specific routing and subtractive exclusion gating.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off is an executable single-channel history-aggregated matrix-factorization control: compute one user vector as the attention-free mean of that user's train-history item embeddings, score candidates by dot product with item embeddings, train with the same BPR objective and embedding tables, and remove both slot routing and exclusion subtraction.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: A GeneralRecommender that uses K=4 fixed-count intent slots formed from attention over each user's train-history items, plus one exclusion prototype and candidate-conditioned routing, compared against an otherwise matched mean-history dot-product control.
research_spec.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does candidate-routed multi-intent user representation with an explicit exclusion channel outperform a matched single-vector collaborative filtering control?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: This should fit within the campaign budget because ML-1M histories are modest, K is small and fixed, and the main added cost is attention pooling over each user's train-history items plus routed full-sort scoring, which remains practical with cached history indices and batched computation.
